lesson.title: Migration, asylum and borders
lesson.summary: Identify migration risk, polygraph, application and identity uses and the travel-document limit.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must distinguish the listed-use enquiry from the product route.

blocks: The **migration use** area covers specified AI used by or on behalf of competent public authorities or Union bodies in migration, asylum and border management, insofar as use is legally permitted.

Point 7(a) covers polygraphs or similar tools. Point 7(b) covers assessing security, irregular-migration or health risk posed by a person entering or already in a Member State. Do not replace these exact functions with a generic border-software label.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 7(a)–(d); Articles 5, 6

blocks: Point 7(c) covers assistance in examining asylum, visa or residence-permit applications and associated complaints concerning eligibility, including evidence-reliability assessments.
Fictional Northbridge authority compares an application-review assistant with that point. A general opening-hours chatbot has different facts from evaluating whether an applicant qualifies.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 7(a)–(d); Articles 5, 6

blocks: Point 7(d) covers detecting, recognising or identifying people in migration/asylum/border management, except verification of travel documents.

The exact travel-document exception is not an exemption for every identity system used at a border. Record what is verified and whether the tool also identifies people or performs another listed assessment.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 7(a)–(d); Articles 5, 6

blocks: A multi-function border platform may engage several points. Record each intended use, public-authority connection, data, person affected and decision influence, then examine the other Article 6 and Article 5 tests.
The high-risk list supplies no independent legal authorisation to collect data or use the system. National and Union law, scope and dates need their own evidence.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 7(a)–(d); Articles 5, 6

questions.prompt: AI assists a competent authority in evaluating an asylum application and its evidence. Which point needs comparison?

options.reason: That point specifies the application-examination function.
That is not an application assessment.

variants.prompt: Which migration listed use concerns eligibility and evidence in asylum, visa or residence applications?

options.reason: That is not an application assessment.

questions.prompt: A supplier claims every border identity tool fits the travel-document exception. What should be checked?

options.blocks: It excludes all border software automatically
options.reason: The exception is narrower than the whole listed area.

options.blocks: The vendor's slogan is sufficient evidence
options.reason: A slogan does not establish the exact purpose.

options.reason: The exception cannot erase separate identity or risk-assessment functions.
